newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan July long-term prime seen cut to 2.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Japan July long-term prime seen cut to 2.7 pct.

text.p: Japan's July long-term prime lending rate is likely to be set at 2.7 percent, down from 2.9 percent for June, traders said on Friday.
The prime rate is applied to loans of one year and longer to Japanese long-term credit banks' most creditworthy clients.

The prime rate is customarily set 0.9 point above the coupon rate of monthly issued five-year debentures by the Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd (IBJ), the benchmark in Japan's debentures market from which these banks raise funds.

The yield of IBJ's 2.0 percent June five-year debentures fell as low as 1.78 percent on Friday, justifying a cut by 0.2 percentage point in the bank's new coupon rate and the new prime lending rate, traders said.
IBJ has said it would announce its coupon rate for July and its new prime rate on Tuesday next week.
"IBJ is likely to cut its debenture coupon rate by 0.2 point to 1.8 percent unless something extraordinary happens," said a dealer at a domestic brokerage house.
The long-term prime rate is reviewed every month, reflecting market trends.
